confidence_boundary: This reverse-owner control proves that the session pair at +0x28D/+0x28E is not the canonical Gate-owner/challenger pair. It does not yet identify the actual canonical owner field or source object.

runtime_observation.launch_method: clean executable launch with normal battery save; no executable save state

supported_conclusions: The active Gate is global Gate ID 21 because both Gate bonus lookups entered 0x02065BF4 with r0 = 21.
Participant index 1 owns Gate ID 21 in this capture because ID 21 appears in participant 1's three Gate-card slots and does not appear in participant 0's slots.
The active Gate therefore belongs to participant index 1 while participant index 0 contests it.
Despite reversed Gate ownership relative to the player-owned control, session +0x28D remained 0 and +0x28E remained 1.
The +0x28D/+0x28E pair is therefore not a canonical owner/challenger encoding.
The pair remains suitable as a combatant-order or participant-order candidate, but those semantics require separate confirmation.

rejected_interpretations.reason: It remained 0 while participant index 1 owned the active Gate ID 21.
It remained 1 while participant index 0 was the participant contesting participant 1's Gate.
